activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
fact: Your name written down has the same letters in the same order every time.
story:
Maeva went to the store with Dad. She wanted a book about fish. Fish swim in the blue water, and Maeva loved that. On the shelf she saw a birthday card. It had letters on it. "M-A-E-V-A," said Maeva. "That is my name!" The letters were red and shiny.

Near the card there was a sticker. It had letters too. "M-A-E-V-A," said Maeva again. One, two, three, four, five letters. The same letters. The same order. Her name looked just the same both times. Maeva put her finger on each letter. M, A, E, V, A.

Then she found the fish book. Dad helped her hold it. They opened the front cover first. On the first page, deep down in the sea, a big fish smiled at her. "Look, Dad," said Maeva. "The fish sees me too!"

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
fact: Asking family to help look means more people are searching.
story:
Athena lost her bunny at daycare. Bunny had soft white ears. Athena looked in the toy box. No bunny there. She looked under the art table. She found a red crayon, but no bunny. Athena felt like crying a little. It was cold outside, almost winter. Bunny could not stay lost.

Her big sister came to pick her up. "I lost Bunny," Athena said. Her sister knelt down. "I will help you look," she said. Then their dad came in too. "I can help too," he said. Now three people were looking.

Dad looked by the coat hooks. Sister looked in the play kitchen. Athena looked near the book shelf. Dad lifted a big green coat. The coat had been hiding something. Bunny was under the coat!

"Bunny!" Athena hugged her tight. Bunny's ear was a little crunchy from a left-over cracker. "We can wash that off at home," said Dad. On the way out, Athena held sister's hand. "Thank you for helping," she said. "More eyes found Bunny," said sister, and she smiled. Athena waved to her teacher. "Bye! See you tomorrow!" she called.

activity: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
knowledge_domain: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
fact: Birds are animals that have feathers.
story:
Isaiah went to the big store with Mama. "Let's find our juice," said Mama. Isaiah held her hand the whole time.

First they walked past the toys. A long train sat on a shelf. Isaiah waved at it. Then they walked past the foods. Apples, bread, and milk were all there.

Then Isaiah saw something on the floor. It was a small feather. It was soft and gray.

Isaiah picked it up. "Mama! Look!" he said.

"Where did that come from?" asked Mama.

Isaiah looked up. A bird sat on a tall shelf. The bird was picking at a big bag of seeds.

"Birds have feathers," said Isaiah. "The bird lost one!"

Mama laughed. "You are right!"

They got the juice. They did not forget the feather. At home, Isaiah put it in his pocket, next to a toy car.

"Feather, meet car," said Isaiah.

activity: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
knowledge_domain: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
fact: At a train station, people wait on the platform and stand back from the edge until the train stops.
story:
Amira ran into the backyard. "Grandma comes today!" she said. Dad said, "We will keep her bag safe in the house." They got in the car. They drove to the train station.

At the station, people stood on the platform. There was a yellow line on the floor. Dad stood behind it. Amira stood behind it too. Then she heard a sound. Choo, choo! She wanted to lean out to see the train. Dad held her hand. "Stand here with me," he said. So Amira stepped back behind the line. The train came in. It went whoosh, whoosh, whoosh. Then it stopped. Only then did the doors open. And there was Grandma!

"One grandma, one big bag, one warm hug," said Amira, counting on her fingers. Grandma laughed. At home, Amira showed Grandma the backyard. "One swing, one sandbox, two sheep in the next yard," said Amira. The sheep said baa. Grandma sat down on the swing. Amira pushed her gently, back and forth, back and forth.

The next day they went back to the station, just to watch. They stood on the platform, behind the yellow line. "Is a train coming soon?" Amira wondered. She heard choo, choo far away. She watched the train stop, all by itself. Then the doors opened. "Again!" said Amira.

activity: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
knowledge_domain: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
fact: Saying 'sorry' shows you feel bad when you hurt someone or make a mistake.
story: Leah sat in her car seat. The car went bump, bump, bump. Her toy bunny sat next to her. One, two, three bumps, and the car turned a corner. Bunny fell on the floor. "Oh no," said Leah. "Sorry, Bunny. Are you okay?" She reached down, but her arms were too short. The seat was deep and she could not reach. "Mom, can you help me, please?" she asked. Mom could not reach either. Dad stopped the car at the red light. He turned around and picked up Bunny. "Thank you, Dad," said Leah. She gave Bunny a big hug. "Bunny makes a joke," she said. "She fell on purpose!" Dad laughed. Then the light turned green, and the car went on. Leah waved Bunny's paw out the window, just a little swing, swing, swing.

activity: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
knowledge_domain: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
fact: It is polite to wait until someone finishes talking before you start to speak.
story:
Owen wanted to tell Miss Lily something big. It was about his birthday cake. It had a blue truck on it. He ran to her at the paint table. Miss Lily was talking to Ben. "Owen," said Miss Lily, "please wait one minute." Owen opened his mouth. Then he closed it. He put his hand on her arm and waited.

Ben told about his windy walk to daycare. The leaves had blown all around. Then Ben stopped talking. Miss Lily looked at Owen. "Now I can listen," she said. Owen took a big breath. "My cake had a blue truck!" he said. "I want to paint a truck." Miss Lily smiled. "Thank you for waiting," she said. "Here is the blue paint."

Owen painted a big blue truck. Ben leaned over. "Can I add a road?" he asked. "Yes, please," said Owen. Ben painted a grey road under the wheels. Owen looked at his picture. "I want to show my mom," he whispered to Miss Lily. "She will hang it up." Miss Lily nodded. "At pickup time," she said. Owen watched the door and waited.

activity: starting the first day of school
knowledge_domain: starting the first day of school
fact: A classroom has rules that everyone in the class follows.
story:
Mya stood at the school gate. The gate was huge. Behind it was her very first day of school.

"Hold my hand," said Mama. "We wait for the teacher."

Mya waited. She counted the gate bars. One, two, three, four. The teacher came and opened the gate. "Hello, Mya! Come in."

Inside, the teacher read a paper out loud. "Our class rules. One, we walk inside. Two, we hang our coats. Three, we sit for stories."

At play time, Mya wanted to ride the toy horse. It was a huge horse, red and shiny. She began to run to it.

A boy named Sam held up his hand. "Stop! We walk inside," he said. Mya stopped walking fast. She walked slow, slow, slow to the horse. Sam laughed. "Slow like a turtle!" Mya laughed too.

At story time, Mya hung her coat on her hook. Then she sat down on the mat.

"Sam," she whispered, "did I do all the rules?" Sam counted on his fingers. "Walk, coat, sit. Yes! All three."

Mya clapped her hands. "I did it!" Then she patted the space next to her. "Sit here, Sam."

Sam sat down, and the teacher opened the book.

activity: learning to play a musical instrument
knowledge_domain: learning to play a musical instrument
fact: You play a guitar by plucking or strumming its strings.
story:
Ryan ran into the music studio. A big guitar sat on a stand. "Can I play it?" he asked.

His teacher, Miss Kim, smiled. "You can try."

Ryan tapped the guitar like a drum. Tap, tap, tap. But the guitar stayed quiet. Only a small thump came out. Ryan frowned. "Why won't it sing?" he asked.

Miss Kim passed him a little pick. "Try brushing the strings," she said.

Ryan held the pick. He brushed it across the strings. Strum! A big, warm sound filled the room.

"Again!" said Ryan. He strummed fast. Then he strummed slow. His tummy felt jumpy with joy.

"Can I show Mom?" he asked.

"Yes," said Miss Kim. "You are ready."

Ryan stood tall and proud. He strummed one more time, loud and happy, all the way to the door.

activity: going on a family trip away from home
knowledge_domain: going on a family trip away from home
fact: On an airplane, people in their seats buckle their seat belts for takeoff and landing.
story:
Zayn was a little boy in a big hotel room. He jumped on the squishy bed. "We fly home today!" said Mama. Zayn slid his small suitcase across the floor. Vroom!

At the airport, Zayn found his seat near the window. The plane began to rumble. Zayn wanted to stand up. He wanted to see out the window now!

"Click, click, click," went the seat belts all around him. Everyone buckled up. Papa buckled Zayn's belt too. "But I want to see!" said Zayn.

The plane went faster and faster. Then it lifted up, up into the sky. Zayn stayed in his seat. He could still see the clouds. "Wow," said Zayn. "I can see from here!"

Mama laughed. "Silly boy, the window came to you." Zayn watched a cloud shaped like a bunny hop past the window.

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
fact: Feelings can show on your face, like a big smile when you are happy.
story:
Arnaud did not want to sleep. He wanted his favorite toy, a soft brown cow. He looked under his bed. The cow was not there. Arnaud's mouth turned down. His face felt sad. He showed his face to Mama. "I see a sad face," she said. "Let us look together."

They looked in the toy box. They looked behind the chair. Then Arnaud heard a sound. "Moo," said the cow, from inside the closet! Arnaud ran to the closet. He hugged his cow. His mouth turned up into a big smile. "I see a happy face now," said Mama.

Then the lamp made a click and went off. The room went dark. Arnaud held his cow tight. His eyes grew wide. "I feel scared," he said. Mama turned on her small light. The room was not dark anymore. Arnaud's eyes got small again. His face felt calm.

Mama held up a little mirror. "Make a face," she said. Arnaud made a happy face. The boy in the mirror smiled too. Arnaud made a grumpy face, like when he was angry at nap time. The boy in the mirror scowled too. Arnaud laughed. The mirror boy laughed.

He put his cow under his arm. He got into bed. Mama kissed his head. "Good night, cow," said Arnaud. "Good night, mirror boy." Then he closed his eyes to sleep.

activity: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
knowledge_domain: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
fact: A week has seven days.
story:
Evelyn went to the park with Dad. Today the ice cream cart was not there. "Where is the ice cream man?" she asked. "He came yesterday," said Dad. "He comes once a week. Tomorrow he will still be far away."

Evelyn wanted ice cream now. "How long is a week?" she asked. Dad held up one hand. "Count the days on your fingers." Evelyn counted. One, two, three, four, five. Then she ran out of fingers. "A week is too big for one hand!" she said. Dad helped her count on his hand too. Six, seven. "A week has seven days," said Dad. "That is a lot of days."

Evelyn played while she waited. She went down the slide. Now it was sunny. Later the sun moved and made a wide shadow by the bench. Evelyn sat in the shadow. "The shadow is big now," she said.

Each day she counted one finger. One day the ice cream man came. He gave her a present, a little spoon with a star on it. Evelyn held it up high. "Seven days are done!" she said. "Can we count them again tomorrow?"

activity: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
knowledge_domain: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
fact: Peas grow inside pods on the plant.
story:
Jules ran to the community garden with his dad. He had little pea seeds in his hand. He wanted to grow big plants, fast!

Jules dug a small hole. He dropped the seeds in. He patted the dirt down. Then he watered the soil. Every day he came back to look.

But nothing grew. Jules looked and looked. Just dirt! His dad said, "Wait, Jules. Watch." So Jules waited. A red ladybug sat on the dirt. A frog hopped near the fence. Then one day, Jules saw something new. A tiny green sprout!

The sprout grew tall. It grew leaves. It grew more and more. Soon there were fat green pods on the plant. Jules picked one pod. He squeezed it. Pop! The pod opened. Inside was a row of little round peas! "Dad, come see! The peas were hiding in here!" Jules picked more pods. He filled his whole bucket. That night, snow peas from Jules's plant sat on his plate. He ate them all up and said, "I grew these myself!"

activity: getting a first haircut at a salon
knowledge_domain: getting a first haircut at a salon
fact: A hairdresser can hold up a hand mirror to show you the back of your hair.
story:
Beatrice sat in a big chair at the mall. It was her first haircut. Mama stood close by her side.

The hairdresser cut with scissors. Snip, snip. Beatrice felt something stick to her sleeve. It was a little piece of hair. She brushed it off, and it fell down.

"Now you look so neat," the hairdresser said. Beatrice wanted to see. She turned her head left. She turned her head right. "I can't see the back," she said. "That is not bad. We can fix it," said the hairdresser.

The hairdresser picked up a small mirror. She held it up behind Beatrice. Beatrice looked in the big mirror. There was the back of her hair! "I see it!" said Beatrice. "Short and neat."

Mama smiled and held out her hand. Beatrice jumped down and took it.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
fact: Words are all around us, on signs, labels and boxes, and they tell us things.
story:
Elijah went to the store with Mama. He wanted a book about trucks. "We can find one," said Mama.

At the door, Elijah saw a big red sign. "What do those words say?" he asked. Mama held his hand. "They say Open," she said. "Words tell us things." A man read the sign too. Then he walked in. The words made him come inside!

Elijah skipped to the book shelf. He found a truck book with a cute dog on the cover. He opened the front cover first. He turned the pages one by one, front to back. Each page had words and big trucks.

At the counter, the lady read the box of stickers. The words said Blue. The stickers were blue, just like the words said. Elijah hugged his book. "Trucks," he read on the cover. "That word says Trucks," said Mama. Elijah smiled. His dream truck book was his.

activity: to recognise the letters of the alphabet and the sound each letter makes
knowledge_domain: to recognise the letters of the alphabet and the sound each letter makes
fact: The English alphabet has 26 letters.
story:
Leah stood by the alphabet chart. Her teacher, Miss Po, pointed at a big red letter.

"This is A," said Miss Po. "A says ah, like apple."

"Ah, ah, apple," said Leah. Then she saw something. Each letter had a picture. B had a ball. C had a cat.

"I want to count them," said Leah.

She tapped each letter with her finger. "One, two, three." Her friend Tom came to help.

"Count with me," said Leah. Tom tapped too. They went all the way down the chart. "Twenty-four, twenty-five, twenty-six!"

Leah jumped up. "Twenty-six letters! That is a lot!"

"Yes it is," said Tom. "Almost as many as my toy cars."

Miss Po laughed. "Now find the letter for your name."

Leah looked hard. "L!" she said. "L says lll, like lion."

"And what does M say?" asked Miss Po. "For Miss Po, my name."

Leah slid her shoe on the floor. "It goes mmm," she said, "like my foot going mmm down the hall."

The bell rang. The door opened. The kids ran out to play.

"Wait!" called Leah. "P! P says puh, like play!"

Tom giggled. "You found it fast."

"Twenty-six letters," said Leah. "I know them all. Almost."

activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
fact: In a very dark room, it is hard to tell what color things are.
story:
Abigail was sleeping at Grandma's house. At bedtime she pulled open the sock drawer. The room was very dark. She felt two socks that seemed the same. She put them on and went to sleep.

In the morning, Grandma opened the curtains. Sunlight filled the room. Abigail looked down at her feet. One sock was red. One sock was green. "Grandma, look!" she said. "They looked the same last night!" Grandma laughed a friendly laugh.

"Try again tonight," said Grandma. Abigail picked new socks in the light. One was blue. One was yellow. She held them up to the window to be sure. Then she laid them by her bed. After her bath, she put them on in the dark. In the morning she peeked under the blanket. Two blue toes. Two yellow toes. "It worked!" said Abigail.

activity: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
knowledge_domain: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
fact: Other languages have their own words for thank you, like 'gracias' in Spanish.
story:
Elena was at Grandma's house. She wanted the cookies on the high shelf. "Please, Grandma, may I have one?" she asked. Grandma smiled and gave her a warm cookie. It smelled like sugar and butter.

Then a boy named Mateo came to play. He lived next door. Grandma gave him a cookie too. "Gracias," said Mateo. Elena stopped chewing. That was a new word! "What did you say?" she asked. "Gracias," said Mateo again. "It means thank you." Elena practiced it in her mouth. "Gra-cias," she said slowly. Mateo laughed, so she said it again.

They ran outside into the cool air. Elena tried to jump over the hose and slipped. She fell in the wet grass. "Sorry," said Mateo, "I moved the hose." Elena felt her knee. "Grandma!" she called. Grandma came fast and washed the little scrape. It did not even hurt much.

They played until the sun went down and it got late. "Say bye to Mateo," said Grandma. Elena waved. "Bye, Mateo! Gracias for playing with me!" Mateo grinned. "De nada," he called back. Elena giggled. A brand new word, again!

activity: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
knowledge_domain: basic time concepts such as yesterday, today, tomorrow, now and later
fact: A clock shows what time it is.
story:
Kinsley sat in her car seat. Today they were going to Grandma's house. Yesterday they had stayed home. Tomorrow they would go to the park.

"Are we there now?" Kinsley asked.
"Not now," said Mom. "Later, when the clock says two."
The clock sat on the car dash. Its little hands moved, tick by tick.

Kinsley watched the clock. She held her book on her lap. The hands moved some more. "Is it later yet?" she asked.
Mom looked. "Look at the clock," she said.
The big hand was at the two now. Right then, the car turned a big corner. There was Grandma's house!

Kinsley climbed down from her seat. Grandma held out a red apple. "A juicy one for you," Grandma said. Kinsley took a big bite. Crunch!

"Can we have pie later?" Kinsley asked.
"Yes," said Grandma. "Later, after lunch."
Kinsley smiled and looked back at the door. The car clock was still ticking away inside.

activity: recovering from a cold or flu at home
knowledge_domain: recovering from a cold or flu at home
fact: When you cough or sneeze, you cover it with your elbow.
story:
Henry was at Grandma's house. He had a little cold. His nose was red and his cough came back and back.

Grandma sat with him by the window. The sky was cloudy. Henry looked at the birds. Then he felt a big sneeze coming. "Ah... ah... achoo!" The sneeze went right into his hand.

Grandma brought a towel and wiped his hand. "Try this," she said. She lifted her arm and made a little cave with her elbow. "Sneeze in here."

Henry wanted to try. He lifted his arm. He made a little cave too. He waited. The sneeze came. "Achoo!" It went into his elbow, not his hand. His hand stayed clean. Grandma clapped softly.

Henry sneezed two more times that day. Each time, up went his arm. Each time, his elbow caught the sneeze. "I did it," he said. Grandma gave him a warm hug and a glass of juice. Henry smiled and took a big sip.

activity: recovering from a cold or flu at home
knowledge_domain: recovering from a cold or flu at home
fact: When you feel sick, you tell a grown-up.
story:
Jules had a cold. His nose was red. His throat felt scratchy.

He sat at the big kitchen table. Mama gave him warm soup. The bowl was too hot. Mama held the spoon herself. Jules blew on the soup. Then he took a tiny sip.

Mama went to the sink. She began to dig in the drawer for a spoon. Jules felt his throat hurt more. He wanted to hide it. But he thought of Grandma's words. Grandma had told him once, "When you feel sick, you tell a grown-up."

"Mama," said Jules. "My throat hurts."

Mama came right away. She touched his head with her hand. "You told me," she said. "That was good." She gave him a little cup of honey. The honey went down slow and sweet.

Jules closed his eyes and rested. Then he heard a tap, tap at the window. A small red bird sat there, looking in at him.

"Hello," said Jules. The bird tapped again.

activity: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
knowledge_domain: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
fact: Pinching your nose shut makes it hard to smell anything.
story:
Harper ran to the farm gate. "I know my five senses!" she said. Grandpa smiled. "Show me," he said.

"First, my eyes!" said Harper. She peeked over the fence. She saw beautiful white sheep. "My eyes see the sheep!" Next, she touched a soft lamb. "My hands feel soft fur," she said. Then she heard a loud moo. "My ears hear the cow!" A sweet smell floated by. It came from the kitchen. Cookies! "My nose smells cookies!" said Harper.

Harper pinched her nose shut. She sniffed and sniffed. She could not smell the cookies at all! She let go of her nose. Sniff, sniff. The sweet smell came back! Harper laughed and laughed. "Grandpa! My nose was off!" she said. "One cookie for my tongue to taste, please." Grandpa handed her a warm cookie. Harper took a big bite. "Mmm! My tongue wins!"

activity: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
knowledge_domain: to name the five senses and say which body part is used for each
fact: There are five senses: seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching.
story:
Layla woke up at Grandma's house in the morning. She smelled something warm. "Grandma, what is that smell?" she asked. "Cinnamon rolls," said Grandma. "My nose smelled them!" said Layla.

Grandma laughed. "Your nose is one sense. Smelling." Layla held up one finger. "One, smelling," she said. Then she touched the soft kitchen towel. "Two, touching with my hands!" She heard the kettle sing. "Three, hearing with my ears!" She saw the pink flowers on the table. "Four, seeing with my eyes!"

Grandma put a small piece of roll on Layla's plate. Layla tasted the sweet cinnamon. "Five, tasting with my mouth!" She counted all five fingers on her hand. "One nose, two hands, two ears, two eyes, one mouth. Five senses!" Grandma clapped. Layla took a big bite of her favorite roll and smiled.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
fact: A pretend tea party can use empty cups with no real tea in them.
story:
Matthew wanted to give his bear a drink. But the water table was empty. There was no water for tea today.

Miss Ana saw Matthew looking sad. She gave him three little cups. The cups were empty too. "Hmm," said Matthew.

Mia sat down next to him. She picked up a cup. She tipped it over her bunny. "Tea for you," said Mia. "Careful, it's pretend hot!" The bunny drank nothing at all. But Mia patted her softly anyway.

Matthew tipped his cup over his bear. Nothing came out. But he made a loud pour sound. "Glug, glug." Bear drank it all up. "More tea?" asked Matthew. He poured again and again.

Soon the cups were stacked up tall. Bear was full of pretend tea. Matthew remembered the shiny coin in his pocket. He put it under a cup. "You pay for tea now," he told Mia. Mia giggled and paid with a pretend coin from the air.

Miss Ana smiled at the quiet tea party. "May I have some tea too?" she asked. Matthew poured her a big pretend cup. "Careful," he said. "It's pretend hot."

activity: recovering from a cold or flu at home
knowledge_domain: recovering from a cold or flu at home
fact: When you have a cold, resting in bed or on the couch helps your body get better.
story:
Arthur had a sniffly nose. He sat on the big couch with his red sock on one foot. His other sock was lost under a pillow.

Arthur wanted to run outside. He slid off the couch. "I want to play ball," he said. Mama picked him up. "Not today," she said. She tucked him in with his bear and his favourite book.

Arthur felt grumpy. His tummy felt sour and his nose was red. He looked out the window. A bird hopped on the grass. Arthur snuggled his bear closer. He read his book, page by page. Soon his eyes felt heavy. He slept for a long, long time.

When Arthur woke up, he sniffed. His nose was better! "I can breathe again," he said. Mama smiled. "Rest helped you," she said. Arthur bounced a little on the couch cushions. He found his lost sock under the pillow. He put it on his foot. Then he hugged his bear and said, "You rest too, bear. Then we both play."

activity: watching a big game with family and friends
knowledge_domain: watching a big game with family and friends
fact: Fans often wear their team's colors to show which team they cheer for.
story:
Oliver was at Grandpa's house. It was the day of the big game. Everyone was coming to watch. Grandpa put on his red shirt. Uncle Ben put on his red shirt too. Aunt Mia wore a red hat.

Oliver looked down at his blue shirt. He wanted red, like everyone else. "Grandpa, I need red," he said. Grandpa looked in the closet. He found a little red shirt. "This was mine when I was small," said Grandpa.

Oliver put it on. It was a bit big, but he wore it anyway. He walked to the couch and sat by Grandpa. Then the doorbell rang. It was their neighbor, Sam. Sam was wearing blue! "Oh no," said Oliver. "Sam cheers for the other team!" Sam laughed and sat on the far side of the room. Grandpa handed out popcorn. The game was just about to start. "Go red team!" Oliver shouted. Sam shouted back, "Go blue!"

activity: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
knowledge_domain: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
fact: Wrapping paper hides a present, so nobody can see what is inside until it is opened.
story:
Victor woke up on his birthday. "Today is my party!" he shouted. Grandma was there. Aunt Lily was there. Ben from next door was there too. On the table sat a big box. It was covered in blue paper with stars. "Is it for me?" asked Victor. "Yes," said Grandma. "But you must wait."

Victor could not wait. He shook the box. He heard something go thump. He squeezed it. Something soft touched his fingers through the paper. "Is it a bear?" he asked. Ben leaned in close. "Maybe it is a truck," said Ben. "What can it be?" They shook it again. Thump, thump. Nobody could see inside.

Then Dad helped Victor open it. The paper came off. The box came open. Inside was a big red bear! "A bear! A bear!" Victor hugged it tight. Ben laughed. Grandma clapped. "Now we know," said Victor. "The paper was hiding him!" The bear wore a little blue hat. Victor put the hat on his own head. "Happy birthday, Victor!" everyone sang.

activity: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
knowledge_domain: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
fact: Watching the ball all the way to your hands helps you catch it.
story:
Brielle stood in the grass at school. Miss Patty, a kind woman with white shoes, held a big red ball. "Now we throw the beanbag in the hoop," she said.

Brielle threw her beanbag. It went to the side. It did not go in the hoop. Tom threw his beanbag. It went in! Tom clapped. Brielle picked up her beanbag. She looked at the hoop. She looked and looked. She threw it again. This time it went in. She had watched the hoop, and the beanbag went in. "I did it!" she said.

Then it was time for the big ball. Miss Patty rolled it to Brielle. Brielle shut her eyes tight. The ball bumped her arm. It rolled away. Tom ran after the ball and brought it back. "Here you go," he said.

Miss Patty rolled the ball again. This time Brielle kept her eyes open. She watched the ball all the way to her hands. She held it with both hands. She caught it!

"Again!" said Brielle. Miss Patty rolled the ball. Brielle watched it all the way. She held it tight. Tom held out his hands too. "My turn!" he said. Brielle rolled the big ball to her friend.

activity: playing on a sports team for the season
knowledge_domain: playing on a sports team for the season
fact: A season is all the practices and games a team plays from start to end.
story:
Natalie put on her red shirt. It was her soccer team shirt. She liked to wear it on game days. Today the team played at the big park.

Natalie kicked the ball to Ben. Ben kicked it back. The ball went into the net. The team cheered. One small kick made a big cheer happen.

After the game, Dad sat on the grass with her. Natalie watched a shy ant crawl on her shoe. She shook her shoe and the ant ran off fast.

"When does soccer stop?" Natalie asked. Dad opened the team paper. It had all the games on it. They counted together. One, two, three games were left. "Then the season is done," said Dad. Natalie looked at the paper. So a season was all those games, from the first one to the last one. She had played some already. Three more were still coming.

The next game, it rained. Natalie slipped in the mud. She got up and kept running. She kicked the ball with her muddy foot. It went to Ben. Ben kicked it in. "Good pass!" Ben said.

On the last game day, the coach gave everyone a ribbon. Natalie held hers up high. "We played the whole season," she said. Dad hugged her. "All the practices and all the games," he said. Natalie spun around with her ribbon in the sun.

activity: starting the first day of school
knowledge_domain: starting the first day of school
fact: When a class walks somewhere together, the children often walk in a line.
story:
Maya stood in the school hallway. It was her very first day. She held her teacher's hand.

"Where do we go?" Maya asked.

"We walk to the music room," said Miss Kim. "Watch. Everyone makes a line."

The children stood one behind the other. Maya did not know where to put herself. She ran ahead to the front door.

Miss Kim shook her head. "Not yet, Maya. Find your spot."

Maya looked back. There was an empty space. It was between Ben and the tall girl with red shoes. Maya stepped into the space. Now she had a spot.

The line started to walk. Maya walked in her spot. Ben walked in front of her. The tall girl walked behind her. Maya could see everyone.

"Like a train," said Maya.

"Yes," said Miss Kim. "You catch on fast."

The line went down the hallway. Maya held her spot all the way. The music room door was open. Inside there was a big rug.

Miss Kim said, "Sand buckets are for play time later. For now, come sit on the rug."

Maya sat down next to Ben. She smiled. School was a good place to be.

activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
fact: Sorting by color means putting all the things that are the same color together in one group.
story:
Natalie was at daycare. It was clean-up time. The block corner was very messy. The sun did shine on the blocks through the window. Natalie made piles. All the red blocks went in one pile. All the blue blocks went in another pile. All the yellow blocks went in a third pile. Then she made a green pile too.

Natalie counted her piles. "Where is my big red block?" she asked. She looked in the red pile. It was not there. She looked at the blue pile. There it was, hiding with the blue blocks. The red block was in the wrong pile. Natalie picked it up. She put it with the red blocks. Now all the red blocks sat together.

Ben played with his toy doctor kit next to her. "My patient needs a red block," he said. Natalie gave him one from the red pile. "All better," said Ben.

activity: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
knowledge_domain: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
fact: Guests who come to stay pack their clothes and things in a suitcase or bag.
story:
Jack stood at the airport with Dad. He waited for Grandma to come. "Her plane will land soon," said Dad. Jack watched the big doors. People came out, one, two, three. Grandma came out last, and she waved.

Grandma had a big red suitcase. "What is inside?" Jack asked. "My clothes and my things," said Grandma. "I will stay with you for one week." Jack helped pull the suitcase. It was heavy. It went bump, bump, bump across the floor.

At home, Grandma opened the suitcase. Out came a shirt, a sweater, and warm socks. Out came a small ant toy for Jack. He laughed and held it tight. Then Grandma put her clothes in the drawer, one, two, three. "Now I am all moved in," she said. Jack hugged her leg and smiled up at her.

activity: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
knowledge_domain: bringing home a first pet and learning to care for it
fact: When a pet is sleeping or eating, it is best to leave it alone.
story:
Wesley stood by a tall cage at the pet store. A small brown puppy looked at him. "That one," said Wesley. "I want that one." Mom smiled and nodded.

At home, the puppy sniffed every corner. Then Mom set down a bowl of food. Wesley wanted to pat the puppy now. He reached out his hand. The puppy growled a tiny growl and kept eating. Wesley stepped back. He watched the puppy eat. He waited and waited. Soon the bowl was empty. "All done," said Wesley. Now the puppy ran to him. It licked his hand and spun in a circle. Wesley laughed. Mom found a soft ball, and they played together on the rug.

Later the puppy curled up in its bed and closed its eyes. Wesley whispered, "Sleepy puppy. I will pat you later." He sat nearby and watched. The puppy's tail wagged once, even in its sleep.

activity: to recognise the letters of the alphabet and the sound each letter makes
knowledge_domain: to recognise the letters of the alphabet and the sound each letter makes
fact: Letters can be written as big capital letters or small lowercase letters.
story:
Mateo went to the library with his mama. He wanted to find the letter A. On the wall, he saw a big A. "There it is!" he said. He patted the wall. The big A felt smooth and cool.

Then he opened a thick book. He looked at the page. He saw a small round letter. "That is not A," he said. He turned the page. He saw it again. "Where is A?" His mama sat down next to him. "Take your time," she said.

A girl at the next table leaned over. "That little one is A too," she said. Mateo looked. He looked again. The small a did not look the same as the big A. But it was the same letter. "Big A, small a," he said softly.

He found B, big and small. He found C, big and small. His finger traced the small c on the page. "Same letter," he said. His mama smiled. "Can we read this one now?" Mateo asked, patting the thick book.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
fact: If you hold a book upside down, the words and pictures look upside down too.
story:
Violet went to the library with her dad. She wanted a book about a boat. She looked on the shelf where the boats might hide. She pulled out a big blue book. It felt smooth and cool in her hands.

Violet sat down on the soft rug. She opened the book. The boat was there, but it looked funny. The boat was upside down. The sail pointed down. The words looked upside down too. They hung from the top of the page like little bats.

Violet felt worried. "This book is broken," she told her dad. Her dad sat down next to her. He was warm and smelled like outside. He said nothing. He just smiled and waited.

Violet looked at the book again. She turned it around in her hands. Now the boat sat up straight. The sail pointed up. The words sat on the lines, quiet and neat. Violet laughed. She had been holding the book upside down!

Violet turned one page, then the next. The boat sailed through the whole book. The last page was empty, just blue water and sky. "The end," said Violet. Dad said, "Time to check it out." Violet held the book the right way up all the way to the desk.

activity: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
knowledge_domain: the five senses and the body parts used for seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching
fact: Your nose has two openings called nostrils.
story:
Wesley came to school early. He smelled something warm and sweet. "What is that smell?" he asked. Miss Pam smiled. "Bread is baking. Come and see." Wesley used his eyes to look. He saw the big oven. A grown-up was the only one near the hot oven, so Wesley stood back with Miss Pam.

"I smell it with my nose," Wesley said. Miss Pam held up a little mirror. "Look at your nose," she said. Wesley looked. He saw two little holes. He counted them. "One, two! My nose has two holes!" Miss Pam laughed. "Those are your nostrils." Wesley touched his nose with his fingers. The holes tickled.

Then Miss Pan clapped her hands and shouted, "The bread is ready!" She took it out with big mitts. The bread sat on a wood board. Wesley touched the board. It was smooth. Miss Pam gave him a small warm piece. He tasted it with his tongue. "Yum!" said Wesley. Then he heard a happy sound. It was his own tummy, rumbling. Everyone laughed.

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
fact: Retracing your steps means going back to each place you went, in order.
story:
Sienna sat in the family car. She held her brown bag. But her toy bunny was gone.

"Where is Bunny?" she asked. Her tummy felt tight.

Mama said, "Let us think. Where did we go today?" Sienna thought hard. "We went to the swings. Then we went to the slide. Then we got in the car."

"Then we go back," said Mama. "Swings first. Slide next. The same way, one stop at a time." Sienna buckled her seat belt. The car started to move.

First stop: the swings. Sienna looked under the swing seat. No bunny. Just sand and a brown leaf.

Next stop: the slide. Sienna ran to the slide. She looked at the top. She looked at the bottom. There, in the grass by the ladder, was Bunny! "Bunny!" Sienna hugged her tight. "Thank you, Mama. Going back the same way found her."

At home, Sienna sat by the warm lamp. Bunny sat in her lap. Mama put a soft blanket over them both.

"Bunny can sleep with me," said Sienna. She gave Bunny one more squeeze.

activity: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
knowledge_domain: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
fact: Music and dancing are part of many celebrations.
story:
Thomas stood by the big door. The hall was full of people. Music played and everyone danced.

Thomas did not dance. He held Grandma's hand. His feet stayed very still. "I wish I could dance," he said softly. But his shoes did not move one bit.

Then Uncle Sam walked by. He was dancing like a wobbly duck. He flapped his arms and spun around. Thomas laughed and laughed. His feet began to tap. Tap, tap, tap. They went all by themselves!

Grandma smiled. "Our feet like the music," she said. She took his hand and they stepped out onto the floor. Step, step, turn. The music was fast now. Thomas spun like Uncle Sam. He wobbled like a duck too.

Outside, the street was dark. It was getting late. But inside, the music played on. Thomas danced and danced. Then he shouted, "Look at me, Uncle Duck!" Uncle Sam quacked back at him.

activity: spending a surprise snow day at home
knowledge_domain: spending a surprise snow day at home
fact: At a sledding hill, children sled sitting up and facing forward with a grown-up watching.
story:
Stella woke up and saw white. Snow! Lots of snow. School was closed, and it was a snow day. She put on her boots and ran to the backyard. Dad made a little hill out of snow. It was small, but Stella loved it.

"I will go down like a penguin!" she said. She lay down on her tummy, head first at the top of the hill. Dad shook his head. "Watch me," he said. Dad sat on the sled. He sat up. He faced forward. He held on with both hands. Then he slid down. "Wheee!"

Stella tried it his way. She sat up. She faced forward. She held on tight. Down she went, fast and smooth. She laughed so hard she fell over in the snow. "Again!" she said. Dad pulled the sled back up the hill. Stella touched the cold snow with her mittens and grinned. "Wheee!" said Dad, and down they went together.

activity: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
knowledge_domain: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
fact: Hugging the ball to your chest helps you hold on to it after you catch it.
story:
Theodore stood in the gym with his teacher, Ms. Rose. He wanted to throw the red beanbag into the big hoop. He aimed and threw. The beanbag hit the floor. "Oh no," said Theodore. Ms. Rose smiled. "Try again," she said. Theodore looked at his hands. He moved his hands down low. He threw the beanbag up and out. It sailed through the hoop. "I did it!" said Theodore.

Then Ms. Rose rolled him a big blue ball. He held out his arms. The ball came fast. It hit his hands and bounced away. He tried again. The ball bounced away again. Theodore frowned and pulled his hat down over his eyes. Then the ball came once more. Theodore caught it and pulled it right to his chest. He hugged it tight. The ball stayed!

"Now we can play," said Ms. Rose. She gave him a crunchy cracker for a snack. Theodore hugged the ball again, just because. "My turn," he said. He spun around and laughed. Ms. Rose clapped her hands. The ball stayed snug against his chest all the way to the snack table.

activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
fact: On a clear, sunny day, the sky looks blue.
story:
Axel sat at the big table. He wanted to paint a picture. Mom put the paint cups out. There was red paint. There was yellow paint. There was green paint. There was gray paint too.

Axel began to paint a house. He used red for the roof. He used green for the grass. Then he wanted to paint the sky. He picked up the gray brush. He made one gray line at the top.

Then Axel looked out the window. The sun was shining bright. The sky outside was not gray. The sky was blue. Axel put the gray brush down. "We need blue," he said.

Mom found a blue paint cup. It was a different cup, just for blue. Axel dipped his brush in it. He painted over the gray line. Now his sky was blue, like outside.

Axel held up his picture. "Look, Mom! My sky is sunny day blue!" Mom smiled and hung it on the wall.
